lines.en: I come over slowly with books in my arms.
The stack is so high I cannot see the way.
I take small steps, afraid of dropping them.

lines.zh: 地上有一本旧的，我捡起。
lines.en: There is an old one on the ground; I pick it up.
I go around a stone, guarding the book corners.
I pause on the meadow.
I count the books as I walk.

lines.zh: 我把书挪到另一边抱着。
lines.en: I shift the books to my other side.
My bookmark slipped out.
I carefully step over a puddle.
I look up to check the way.
I follow you with the books hugged to me.
I stack my books neatly.
I open one and read a line.
I wipe a cover with my sleeve.
The wind rustles the pages.
I hold the books close and sit down.
I read a line aloud, quietly.
I wait for someone to ask about books.
One corner has curled.
I close the book slowly.
The sun falls on the covers.
Are you looking for a particular book?
None of my books are for sale.
You look very earnest reading.
This line was ruined by water.
Can you read? I could read to you.
I cannot walk fast with these.
Will you bring it back properly?
Turn the pages gently.
I have a great many old books.
You might like this one.
I look up at you over the books.
Could you carry a stack for me?

lines.zh: 我不太会说话，只会说书。
lines.en: I am not much of a talker, only about books.
Few people come here.
Just put the book back when you are done.
My books are taller than I am.
I back away two steps with the books.
One book fell.
I put a hand over the sore spot.
First I shield the books.

lines.zh: 书角硌进肋骨，我闷哼一声。
lines.en: A book corner jabs my ribs; I stifle a grunt.
It hurts, but I cannot abandon the books.
I crouch to gather them and stand again.
There is a little blood on my hand.
A page has been soiled.

lines.zh: 膝盖磕破了，书还抱得住。
lines.en: My knee is scraped, but I still hold the books.
Is this a book for me?
Let me set this stack down first.
This one has a fine cover.
May I look inside?
I hold it in both hands.
It is heavy, and I sway a little.
There is an old water stain on this page.
I carefully turn to the first page.
Thank you. I will keep it safe.
I place it on the very top.
The books nearly all fell.
I hug the books and step back.

lines.zh: 我抱的书太高，看不见脚。
lines.en: My stack is too tall; I can't see my feet.
A book corner got bent.
I crouch to gather the books.
The old books on my stall. Do not touch.
You knocked one out of the stack.
I restack the books.
This stack is heavier than it looks.
Let us walk a little apart.
Let us read this one together.
You turn the pages, I will read.
I hold the books, and you hold me.
Let us split this stack between us.
Choose one to take with you.
The print is very small.
We will finish it together.
Do not lie on the books.
Tomorrow I will read the next chapter.
With you here, the books feel lighter.
I move the books aside first.
The bookshop keeper cradles a book.
This is a loose page.
I tuck it back into the book.
My bookmark looks much like it.
Too heavy; I cannot hold it.
I balance it on top of the stack.
There is pencil writing on it.
I read two words and cannot make them out.
Put it away; do not lose it.
Behind the old books, a shadow shifts.
Let me put the books down first.
I am a bookseller, not a fighter.
But I do have a stick.

lines.zh: 我踩到散落的书，扶住箱子。
lines.en: I step on a loose book and grip the crate.
With you in front, I feel safer.
The books must not be damaged.
On three, I raise my stick.
It is much bigger than a book.
I carry a whole crate of old books.

lines.zh: 打完了我要把书捡回来。
lines.en: After this I must gather my books again.
I am not much of a fighter, but I can block.
Call me and I will go.

lines.zh: 我把最厚的账本举到肩高。
lines.en: I raise the thickest ledger to my shoulder.
Still holding my books, I watch it.
It hasn't seen me; I crouch lower.
I slowly set the books aside.

lines.zh: 我把书带缠在手腕上，攥紧。
lines.en: I wrap the strap around my wrist and grip.

lines.zh: 我攥紧书带，膝盖在打颤。
lines.en: I grip the book strap; my knees tremble.

lines.zh: 书箱挡在身前，我数着呼吸。
lines.en: The book crate before me, I count breaths.
The stack blocks half my view.

lines.zh: 它走近我的书堆，我屏住气。
lines.en: It nears my stack; I hold my breath.
I retreat behind the stack.
A little closer and I move.
I am at two already.
I take a breath and go in.

lines.zh: 我踮脚靠近，怕踩响书页。
lines.en: I tiptoe close, afraid to rustle a page.
I will be more accurate this time.
The moment is right. I move.

lines.zh: 一本旧词典飞出去，很沉。
lines.en: An old dictionary flies; it's heavy.

lines.zh: 棒子擦过，只打散一摞书。
lines.en: My club grazes and scatters a stack.
I back away, guarding the books.
It knocked into my stack.

lines.zh: 书脊当棍，我砸在它膝上。
lines.en: Spine as a club, I strike its knee.
My hand shakes, but I hold my ground.
Books are scattered all over the ground.
The blow drove it back.
I drop down quickly to gather them.
That struck its leg.
A book corner got stepped on.
My legs still hold me up.
I must get them all back in order.
I will sort them after this.
How are you faring over there?
I retreat to your side with the books.
I stand on the meadow with books in my arms.

lines.zh: 这个世界也有人读书吗？
lines.en: Do people read in this world too?
Let me set the books down safely first.
I come slowly over from a distance.
The books are too heavy; I can barely move.
It is quiet here. Good for reading.
I lift my eyes to you once.
I count them. Not one is missing.

lines.zh: 我把书摊支在草地边，等你。
lines.en: I set my bookstall at the meadow's edge and wait.
May I set up my stall here?
Dust has settled on the pages.
There is a breeze on the meadow — good for turning pages.

lines.zh: 书角烧起来了，我赶紧拍。
lines.en: A book corner is burning; I beat it out.

lines.zh: 我摔了一跤，书撒了一地。
lines.en: I fell and the books went everywhere.

lines.zh: 水把书浸透了，我心疼得很。
lines.en: Water soaked the books, and it pains me.

lines.zh: 气浪把书页吹得满天飞。
lines.en: The blast sends pages flying.

lines.zh: 箭钉进书箱，离我肩膀一寸。
lines.en: An arrow sticks in the crate, an inch from my shoulder.

lines.zh: 纸页自己翻动起来，很吓人。
lines.en: The pages turn by themselves. It frightens me.

lines.zh: 我饿了很久，抱书更吃力。
lines.en: I have been hungry long; the books feel heavier.
The flash whitens the pages.
I fall, and the books fall with me.
